verified_repairs: The legacy absence fixture now derives both device and mount ID from its actual parent; all checked-in suites pass from the clean detached verifier worktree.

Root-backed and /dev/shm present/absent traversal, authenticated boundary selection, wrong device/mount, symlink, simulated nested bind, pre-boundary substitution, late mount-ID rebound and parent/name replacement checks remain fail closed.
The exact R3 first-reseal same-inode write and target-directory rebound attacks now reject.
Candidate, prepare.py, observer, gate wrappers, launcher, guard, checkpoint verifier and comparator remain byte frozen; pending authority is false and G1/G2 remain absent and locked.

release_blockers.finding: The added second recursive seal does not make the terminal operation joint. The second snapshot_tree_revalidate is followed only by _revalidate_chain, which checks the target's lexical ancestor directories but neither re-hashes regular files nor rewalks nested directory membership. Mutations at the second-seal return boundary therefore false-pass with stale receipts.
evidence: Independent same-inode/same-size attack mutated artifact bytes AAAA to BBBB after the second snapshot_tree_revalidate returned. snapshot_path returned PASS with SHA-256 63c1dd951ffedf6f7fd968ad4efa39b8ed584f162f46e715114ee184f8de9201 while the live file digest was 4a8d8134f29b0b7b60c126f5532bc9f5d9bb73037373cf6fb872d81f1dcefdfd.

Independent nested-membership attack inserted nested/late after the second snapshot_tree_revalidate returned. snapshot_path returned PASS whose entries omitted nested/late while the live authorized tree contained it.

A target-directory rename/replacement at that same boundary is rejected by the final chain check, proving the gap is specifically unsealed file content and nested membership rather than the lexical root name.
storage_contract.py:731-738 performs seal, chain, seal, chain; the trailing chain has no recursive content or nested-membership validation.
release_blockers.impact: Root-cache and tmpfs output/cache evidence can still return PASS while exact content or nested membership at the authorized lexical tree differs from the receipt, defeating the unchanged-root-cache and exact artifact gates.
release_blockers.required_invariant: The terminal publication boundary must jointly bind the pinned mount-aware lexical chain, current target-name identity, exact recursive membership and same-descriptor file bytes. There may be no trailing validation step that covers only names/ancestors while leaving content or nested membership unsealed through return.
release_blockers.minimal_repair: Add deterministic attacks at the final (not first) recursive-seal return boundary for same-inode same-size writes and nested insert/delete/replace. Redesign the terminal seal/publication operation so those attacks reject and the returned receipt is derived from the final jointly authenticated state, rather than adding another alternating content-only or chain-only pass.
